link.was_probably_leader: {border_router} was coordinating your Thread network. When the coordinator disappears, the other devices need a while to agree on a new one.
link.cause_unknown: No clear cause was recorded. Nothing was switched off and no bridge disappeared right before.
link.mesh_split: For {duration}, your Thread devices were split into separate groups that could not reach each other, until they agreed on a new coordinator.
link.new_leader: Your Thread devices had to choose a new coordinator. That took {duration}.
link.mesh_trouble_impact: During that time some devices did not respond, and adding a new device fails almost certainly.
link.pairing_failed_meanwhile: An attempt to add a device failed at the same time - very likely because of this.
link.border_router_gone_impact: Your Thread devices have one way less into your home network. If it was the last one, none of them can be reached.
link.border_router_on_switch: Every time {switch} was switched off, {border_router} disappeared shortly after – and came back once {switch} was on again. This happened {count} times.
link.border_router_on_switch_impact: Each time, your Thread network loses a bridge and may have to choose a new coordinator. Devices stop responding for a while, and adding devices fails in that time.
link.mesh_disturbed_during_pairing: Your Thread network was unsettled at exactly that time, so the new device could not be reached reliably.
link.pairing_stopped: The attempt stopped at this stage: {phase}.
link.pairing_failed_impact: The device is not part of Home Assistant. It may still believe it belongs somewhere and needs a reset before the next attempt.
link.weak_signal: {device} hears its nearest neighbour {neighbour} only faintly ({rssi} dBm).
link.weak_signal_impact: Commands arrive late or not at all, and the device may drop out now and then.
link.weak_signal_battery: Battery devices also run down faster, because they have to repeat themselves.
link.mesh_disturbed: Your Thread network was unsettled at that moment.
link.device_unreachable_impact: You cannot control it and its values are not updated.
link.device_flaky: {device} was briefly away {count} times in the last 24 hours.
link.device_flaky_impact: Commands sent in those moments get lost, and its values lag behind.
link.docker_ipv6_off: IPv6 is switched off for Docker. Home Assistant OS then does not forward IPv6.
link.forwarding_off_seen: When it started, Home Assistant's Thread bridge reported that IPv6 forwarding is off.
link.forwarding_off: Home Assistant does not pass messages between your home network and the Thread network.
link.forwarding_off_impact: New Thread devices cannot be added – the phone stops while checking the Thread connection. Existing devices usually keep working.
link.ipv6_static: IPv6 is set by hand on {interface}.
link.ipv6_no_routes: Home Assistant then ignores the ways into the Thread network that your bridges announce in your home network.
link.ipv6_impact: Home Assistant cannot reach Thread devices, and new ones cannot be added.
link.channel_busy_cause: A lot is going on on the same radio channel – usually Wi-Fi or Zigbee, sometimes a microwave oven.
link.channel_busy: Home Assistant's bridge could not send {count} times in {minutes} minutes because the channel was busy.
link.channel_busy_impact: Messages get lost or arrive late; devices react sluggishly.
link.radio_fault: Home Assistant's Thread bridge lost contact with its radio stick.
link.radio_fault_impact: While that lasts, nothing goes through this bridge. Without another bridge, no Thread device can be reached.
link.otbr_detached: Home Assistant's bridge no longer hears any other Thread device.
link.otbr_disabled: Home Assistant's bridge is not part of any Thread network.
link.otbr_outside_impact: Home Assistant reaches no Thread device through this bridge. Other bridges step in if you have any.
link.route_missing: Home Assistant found no way to the addresses of your Thread devices.
link.route_probably_missing: Your Thread network itself was calm, and no bridge disappeared. Home Assistant has probably lost its way into the Thread network.
link.thread_wave: {count} of {total} Thread devices became unreachable almost at the same moment.
link.thread_wave_impact: You cannot control these devices from Home Assistant. In your phone's home app they often still work.
link.relay_gone: {relay} is no longer reachable. Other devices were connected to your network through it.
link.relay_impact: These devices have to find a new way into the network. Some manage within minutes, some only after a long time, some not at all.
link.server_forgot: The Matter Server knew {count} devices and now knows none.
link.server_forgot_impact: No Matter device can be reached. The devices themselves are fine, but the keys to them are gone.
link.weak_wifi: {device} is far from its access point ({rssi} dBm).

origin.person_unknown: by someone in the Home Assistant app
origin.unknown: (directly on the device, or by something Home Assistant could not identify)

pairing.first_contact: The phone or Home Assistant could not start talking to the device. Usually it is too far away, not in pairing mode, or still paired elsewhere.
pairing.prepare: The device accepted the first contact but stopped responding while it was being set up. Usually the radio connection is poor at that spot.
pairing.authenticity: The device could not prove that it is a genuine certified product, or the certificate could not be checked.
pairing.keys: Handing the device the key to your home did not work. Often the device still holds keys from an earlier attempt.
pairing.network: The device could not join your Thread or Wi-Fi network. Often no router is close enough where the device is.
pairing.find_again: The device joined your network, but Home Assistant could not find it there afterwards. Usually the device is too far from the nearest Thread router or bridge.
pairing.finish: Everything was nearly done, but the last confirmation did not arrive.

pairing_reason.credentials: The Matter Server does not know your Thread network's credentials and could not hand them to the device.
pairing_reason.already_paired: The device is still tied to an earlier setup.
pairing_reason.untrusted: The device's certificate is not recognised – it may be a test or development device.
pairing_reason.invalid_noc: The device rejected the key Home Assistant gave it.
pairing_reason.unreachable: Home Assistant had no way to the device's address.
pairing_reason.not_found: The device could not be found in the network.
pairing_reason.timeout: Setting it up took too long, and the device gave up.

fix.keep_border_router_powered: Plug {border_router} into an outlet that is always on, not into {switch}. It uses very little power when idle and your whole Thread network depends on it.
fix.check_border_router_power: Check that {border_router} has power and is connected to your network. Restarting it once usually helps.
fix.mesh_trouble_rare: Nothing to do if this happens rarely. If it happens often, check that your bridges (speakers, TV boxes, hubs) have power all the time.
fix.pairing_wait_for_mesh: Wait a minute until your network has settled, then try again.

pairing.first_contact: Hold the phone close to the device, put the device into pairing mode again, and check that it is not still added to another app.
pairing.prepare: Try again close to where the device will stay. If that fails, plug a Thread device that is always powered (for example a smart plug) in between.
pairing.authenticity: Update the device's firmware if the maker offers one. If it keeps failing, the device may not be certified for use outside the maker's app.
pairing.keys: Reset the device to factory settings before the next attempt.
pairing.network: Make sure a Thread router or bridge is nearby - for example a smart plug or a speaker - or bring the device closer for pairing.
pairing.find_again: Pair the device closer to a bridge or an always-powered Thread device. Once added, you can move it back.
pairing.finish: Check whether the device appeared in Home Assistant after all. If not, reset it and try again.

fix.pairing_reset_and_retry: Before trying again: reset the device to factory settings, then scan the code again.
fix.weak_signal: Put a Thread device that is always powered (for example a smart plug) between {device} and {neighbour}, or move {device} a little closer.
fix.device_unreachable: Check that {device} has power - or fresh batteries. If it runs on batteries, take them out for ten seconds and put them back.
fix.device_flaky: Check where {device} sits: a mains-powered Thread device nearby (a smart plug, for example) almost always helps. If not, look for a firmware update.
fix.enable_docker_ipv6: Open the terminal in Home Assistant, enter ha docker options --enable-ipv6=true and then restart the whole system (Settings → System → Restart → Reboot system).
fix.forwarding_update_os: This affects certain versions of Home Assistant OS. Check whether an update is available, then restart the system.
fix.ipv6_automatic: Set IPv6 to “Automatic”: Settings → System → Network → {interface} → IPv6.
fix.channel_busy: Move the Thread channel away from Wi-Fi and Zigbee: Settings → Devices & services → Thread → Configure → change channel. Channel 25 sits between the usual Wi-Fi channels.
fix.radio_fault: Plug the radio stick into a USB extension cable, away from the computer and from USB 3 ports. Update its firmware. If it keeps happening, replace the stick.
fix.otbr_detached: This usually sorts itself out. If it lasts, restart the OpenThread Border Router app and check that its radio stick is plugged in.
fix.otbr_disabled: The bridge has no Thread network. Open Settings → Devices & services → Thread and check that a preferred network is set.
fix.thread_wave: Restart your bridges (a HomePod or Apple TV, for example). If that does not help, restart Home Assistant. If it happens again, check that IPv6 in Home Assistant is set to “Automatic”.
fix.relay: Check that {relay} has power. A second mains-powered Thread device nearby means the others no longer depend on this one.
fix.server_restore_backup: Restore the backup of the Matter Server app (Settings → System → Backups). All devices come back at once – pairing each one again is the last resort.

pairing_reason.credentials: Set a preferred Thread network in Home Assistant (Settings → Devices & services → Thread) and add the device through the companion app again.
pairing_reason.already_paired: Reset the device to factory settings, or first remove it from the app it was in before.
pairing_reason.untrusted: Look for a firmware update. The Matter Server only accepts devices with a recognised certificate.
pairing_reason.invalid_noc: Reset the device to factory settings and try again. If it happens again, ask the manufacturer for a firmware update.
pairing_reason.unreachable: Check that IPv6 in Home Assistant is set to “Automatic” and that a bridge is in the same network as Home Assistant.
pairing_reason.not_found: Put the device into pairing mode again and keep the phone close to it. Are the phone and Home Assistant in the same network?
pairing_reason.timeout: Try again closer to a bridge or a mains-powered Thread device.

fix.weak_wifi: Move {device} closer to an access point, or put an access point near {device}. Make sure the device is on the 2.4 GHz network – it reaches further than 5 GHz.

prepare.name: Preparation
prepare.what: The device gets basic settings such as region and time.

authenticity.name: Authenticity check
authenticity.what: Home Assistant checks that the device is a genuine certified product.

keys.name: Key handover
keys.what: The device receives the key to your home and its permissions.

network.name: Joining the network
network.what: The device connects to your Thread or Wi-Fi network.

find_again.name: Finding it on the network
find_again.what: Home Assistant looks for the device on your network.

finish.name: Finishing
finish.what: The device confirms it is ready.
